policy_title: Maintain Roads, Tackle Potholes, and Address Car Insurance Costs
stated: Labour commits to maintaining and renewing the UK's road network, fixing an additional one million potholes across England annually by deferring the A27 bypass. The party will also work to tackle the soaring cost of car insurance for drivers.

source.quote: Our road network is plagued by long-promised projects that are never delivered. The potholes cratering our roads are a visible sign of the decline after 14 years of Conservative rule. Labour will maintain and renew our high-road network, to ensure it serves drivers, cyclists and other road users, remains safe, and tackles congestion. We will fix an additional one million potholes across England in each year of the next parliament, funded by deferring the A27 bypass, which is poor value for money. Labour will further support drivers by tackling the soaring cost of car insurance.

bearing_set.reason: Explicitly targets soaring car insurance costs, a recurring household bill that directly affects real disposable income, particularly for lower-income drivers who depend on a car.

Pothole repair directly reduces road hazards; poor road surfaces cause accidents, injuries and deaths—especially for cyclists and motorcyclists—so material road-safety effects earn a real verdict here.

Road network quality has documented effects on logistics, business transport costs, commuting efficiency, and aggregate productivity; large-scale pothole repair affects real living standards and economic opportunity across the road-dependent economy.

membership_note: Car insurance and road maintenance are the two substantive levers: one bears on household cost of essentials (O2), the other on aggregate productivity and living standards (O13). The funding mechanism (deferring the A27 bypass) is a capital reallocation within existing budgets rather than new borrowing, so it does not clearly move O12's debt-sustainability indicators. No other fundamental clears the non-negligible bar.
